title: Combining metadata filters with vector search

videos.script: A customer reading the Portuguese help pages asks how to return a book. The search should answer in Portuguese. {{question}} So you take the three nearest articles and keep the Portuguese ones. There are none left. {{empty}} The three nearest were all in English, and the filter came too late. {{late}} This lesson is about where a filter goes. After the search, it throws away results you already paid for. Before the search, it is exact, and it costs more as the subset grows. {{before}} You will watch PostgreSQL do the first without telling you. Ask for ten Portuguese rows through an HNSW index, and get one, or none. {{pgvector}} Then you will see how Chroma, LanceDB and Qdrant take a filter, and which of them can be told where to put it. {{engines}} Last, the filter that must never be left out. When two shops share one table, the shop is not a search option. It is a security boundary. {{tenants}} The database should enforce it, not the request. {{end}}
